description: The DSL text of one diagram frame: what was authored while the canvas still matches it, else text regenerated from the canvas (`edited: true`); either way it names the palette, so the text alone redraws the diagram. `canvasEdits` lists what was changed on the canvas against the authored text: recolours, moves, resizes, renames, icons, rewired or bent connectors, and shapes added or removed. Each has `carry`: attributes to merge into that node's existing `[ … ]` list (one list per node) to keep the edit, or null when the language cannot say it. `canvasEdits` is null, with `canvasEditsNote` saying why, when it could not be compared. `losses` names what the language cannot say at all. update_diagram drops anything the text you send does not carry. `revision` names the text the diagram was drawn from (create_diagram and update_diagram return it too), null for a frame with no authored text; canvas edits do not change it. Pass it back as `since` and `dsl` is left out: `dslDiff` is a unified diff of the canvas against that text, both re-serialized the same way so only real changes show, empty while the canvas matches. Line numbers refer to the canonical text (what `get_diagram` returns without `since`), not your original source. Edits the text does not say, such as moves, are only in `canvasEdits`. When `since` is not the current `revision` (the diagram was redrawn from other text since), or there is nothing to compare against, the whole `dsl` comes back with `dslDiffNote` saying why.

documentId.description: File-mode document id from openflow_open or openflow_create; omit to use the paired editor (or, in file mode, the document opened or created last).

frameId.description: Diagram frame id, from create_diagram or list_diagrams. Defaults to the first diagram on the page.

pageId.description: Page to read (see list_pages); defaults to the page the editor shows, or the first page in file mode.

since.description: The `revision` of the text you hold, from create_diagram, update_diagram or an earlier get_diagram. Returns `dslDiff`, a unified diff of the canvas against that text, instead of the whole `dsl`; the whole `dsl` again if it is not the current `revision` (the diagram was redrawn from other text since). Line numbers refer to the canonical text (what `get_diagram` returns without `since`), not your original source.

name: get_diagram
title: Read diagram
